card.name: Period after NSAID boxed warning sentence
card.fires_on: The period ending the sentence "which can be fatal" in NSAID boxed warnings about cardiovascular thrombotic events and gastrointestinal bleeding. Also a comma after "on average" in a fetal renal warning.

modes.label: Period after "can be fatal"
modes.description: Sentence-ending period closing a serious cardiovascular or GI risk statement in a boxed warning.
modes.example: an increased risk of serious cardiovascular (CV) thrombotic events, including myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke, which can be fatal<<.>> Based on available data, it is unclear

modes.label: Comma after "on average"
modes.description: Comma in a fetal renal dysfunction warning, before the time to onset.
modes.example: These adverse outcomes are seen, on average<<,>> after days to weeks of treatment, although

card.plain: It marks the end of the NSAID boxed-warning sentence saying the serious events can be fatal.
